artists.biography:
Tori Amos (born Myra Ellen Amos; August 22, 1963) is an American pianist, singer-songwriter and composer. She is a classically trained musician and possesses a mezzo-soprano vocal range. Amos originally served as the lead singer of 1980s synthpop group Y Kant Tori Read, and as a solo artist was at the forefront of a number of female singer-songwriters in the early 1990s. She was also noteworthy early in her solo career as one of the few alternative rock performers to use a piano as her primary instrument. Some of her charting singles include "Crucify", "Silent All These Years", "God", "Cornflake Girl", "Caught a Lite Sneeze", "Professional Widow", "Spark", "1000 Oceans", and "A Sorta Fairytale", her most commercially successful single in the U.S. to date.
 
As of 2005, Amos had sold 12 million albums worldwide. She has been nominated for several awards, including 8 Grammy Award nominations. Amos was also named one of People Magazine's 50 Most Beautiful People in 1996.

perplexity.description:
In Times of Dragons is the eighteenth studio album by Tori Amos, released on May 1, 2026, through Fontana Records—her first full-length project in over four years following 2021's Ocean to Ocean. The album presents a metaphorical narrative about the struggle between democracy and tyranny, with Amos describing it as a reflection of contemporary political turmoil through the lens of a dystopian fantasy. The conceptual framework follows the artist's journey as she flees from antagonistic forces, encountering various characters along the way, including a pivotal figure called "The Daughter" whose relationship with the narrator culminates in the track "Stronger Together". The album's cover art, created in collaboration with photographer Kasia Wozniak, features a composite of multiple photographs of the artist.

The ten-track album showcases Amos's signature blend of rock and pop sensibilities with introspective piano-driven arrangements. Notable tracks include the title track "In Times of Dragons," "Provincetown," "St. Teresa," and "Gasoline Girls," with three songs—"Veins," "Strawberry Moon," and "Song of Sorrow"—co-written with Natashya Hawley. The album's sonic landscape balances the artist's lyrical storytelling with compelling musical arrangements, creating what reviewers have described as "solid" songs within a "weird but compelling" dystopian narrative where real-life anxieties are amplified and transformed.

This release marks a significant moment in Amos's 36-year career, which has achieved over 12 million records sold, eight Grammy nominations, and countless accolades. In Times of Dragons demonstrates her continued artistic evolution and willingness to engage with contemporary political themes through imaginative, allegorical songwriting.
